question: Which statement best describes Ternary operator?
options: A guard clause handles an early case before the main page content. A component might show a loading message, then return before rendering the results. It is like checking your ticket before boarding.
A ternary chooses one of two results: `condition ? yes : no`. Use it when the page needs an either-or choice, like showing Sign in or Sign out. It works like a two-way signpost.

The `&&` operator shows the element on its right only when the left side is true. Use it for show-or-hide choices, like showing a badge when a message is new. It is like a door that opens only when a condition is met.
A component can return `null` when nothing should appear. For example, a private panel can stay hidden from signed-out visitors. It is like choosing not to put a card on the table.
explanation: A ternary chooses one of two results: `condition ? yes : no`. Use it when the page needs an either-or choice, like showing Sign in or Sign out. It works like a two-way signpost.
